claims.claim: Cyprian put off deciding the case of the lapsed until the bishops could meet, and the Roman clergy, without a bishop, agreed; Cyprian says Novatian wrote their letter
claims.witness: Cyprian, Letter to Antonianus 4-5 (anf05 l.33479-33499; Hartel Ep. 55)

claims.claim: Felicissimus and five presbyters broke with Cyprian (Cyprian: Fortunatus 'one of the five presbyters who some time back deserted from the Church'; Felicissimus 'the standard-bearer of sedition'); Hefele: the party took for its war-cry the bishop's severity toward the lapsed
claims.witness: Cyprian, Letter to Cornelius 9 (anf05 l.34756-34764); Hefele I, sec. 5 (hefele_history-of-the-councils-v1-to-nicaea_clark1872 l.6336-6361)

claims.claim: Some of the lapsed were pressing to receive communion before any decision
claims.witness: Cyprian, Letter to Antonianus 4 (anf05 l.33466-33468)

claims.claim: Cyprian returned to Carthage after Easter 251, after an absence from February 250
claims.witness: Hefele I, sec. 5 (hefele_history-of-the-councils-v1-to-nicaea_clark1872 l.6305-6306, 6365-6366)

claims.claim: The Carthage council met in 251, probably in May; the Rome council probably in October 251. Leclercq: May 251 'absolument certaine', after Monceaux
claims.witness: Hefele I, sec. 5 (hefele_history-of-the-councils-v1-to-nicaea_clark1872 l.6366-6369, 6484); McGiffert's note to Eusebius VI.43.2 follows Hefele (npnf201 l.38275-38281); Leclercq's note 4 (hefele-leclercq_...slice-fra_1907 l.138-140)

claims.claim: A large number of African bishops met, weighed Scripture on both sides, and chose a middle course: hope not denied to the lapsed, long penance, each case examined
claims.witness: Cyprian, Letter to Antonianus 6 (anf05_hippolytus-cyprian-caius-novatian l.33506-33524; Hartel l.7600-7616)

claims.claim: Those who took certificates were to be admitted after examination; those who sacrificed were to be helped at death
claims.witness: Cyprian, Letter to Antonianus 17 (anf05 l.33781-33783; Hartel l.7978-7980)

claims.claim: The decisions were collected in a little book, now lost
claims.witness: Cyprian, Letter to Antonianus 6 (anf05 l.33521-33524); Leclercq's note 6, 'De ce concile, rien ne reste' (hefele-leclercq_...slice-fra_1907 l.145)

claims.claim: Felicissimus and five presbyters were 'lately excommunicated by the judgment of our fellow-bishops', who wrote of it to Cornelius 'last year'
claims.witness: Cyprian, Letter to Cornelius on Fortunatus and Felicissimus 9 (anf05 l.34756-34764); Hefele I, sec. 5 (l.6370-6372) places it at this council

claims.claim: Cornelius, 'holding a council with very many bishops', concurred with Carthage
claims.witness: Cyprian, Letter to Antonianus 6 (anf05 l.33525-33529; Hartel l.7614-7615)

claims.claim: Sixty bishops and many more presbyters and deacons met at Rome; Novatian and his followers were declared strangers to the church; the fallen were to be healed with the medicines of repentance
claims.witness: Eusebius VI.43.2, from Cornelius's letters, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.38272, 38288-38299)

claims.claim: Novatian wrote to the churches that those who had sacrificed should not be admitted to the mysteries, and their pardon left to God
claims.witness: Socrates IV.28, reporting Novatian's letters (npnf202 l.14083-14090)

claims.claim: Dionysius of Alexandria wrote to Novatian, 'For it were better to suffer everything, rather than divide the Church of God'; brief's rendering from the Greek: 'It would have been right to suffer anything at all rather than split the Church of God'
claims.witness: Eusebius VI.45, quoting the letter, tr. McGiffert (npnf201 l.38922-38925); Greek ed. Schwartz-Mommsen (eusebius_werke-bd2-2-...schwartz-mommsen1908 l.7363-7364), Rufinus l.7434-7435; second reading 'minor' (renderings/comparison.md E39)

claims.claim: Fabius of Antioch seemed to lean toward Novatian's party
claims.witness: Eusebius VI.44 (npnf201 l.38829)

claims.claim: When 'the day of another trouble is again beginning to draw near', the African bishops decided 'that peace is to be given' to those who had not ceased to repent; Hefele dates the council to May 252
claims.witness: Synodal letter of the African bishops to Cornelius 1 (anf05 l.34273-34299, ANF Ep. 53); Hefele I, sec. 5 (l.6505-6506)

claims.claim: Novatian's church kept its strict discipline in Phrygia and Paphlagonia in Socrates's day
claims.witness: Socrates IV.28 (npnf202 l.14057-14061)

claims.claim: McGiffert: Cornelius's epistles to Fabius 'are no longer extant'
claims.witness: McGiffert's note to Eusebius VI.43.3 (npnf201 l.38324)

claims.claim: Novatus (Novatian), a presbyter of the church at Rome, held there was no hope for the fallen and led those who called themselves Cathari; Socrates: he was raised to the episcopate by bishops of the same mind, after Cornelius received those who had sacrificed
claims.witness: Eusebius VI.43.1 (npnf201 l.38265-38270); Socrates IV.28, tr. Zenos (npnf202 l.14068-14081)

claims.claim: Dionysius later reported that 'the churches everywhere had rejected the novelty of Novatus, and were at peace among themselves'
claims.witness: Eusebius VII.5 (npnf201 l.39347-39348)

claims.claim: Nicaea, canon 8: ordained Cathari who come over continue in the clergy, if they profess in writing to communicate with 'those who having lapsed in persecution have had a period [of penance] laid upon them'
claims.witness: Council of Nicaea, canon 8, tr. Percival (npnf214_seven-ecumenical-councils l.3767-3775)

claims.claim: Socrates's history runs down to 439; Zenos speaks of 'his favorable attitude towards Novatianism'
claims.witness: Zenos's introduction to Socrates (npnf202 l.886-892, 1064-1065)

contested_claims.claim: Whether a synod at Antioch on the Novatians met
contested_claims.sides: Eusebius VI.46 says Dionysius was invited to the synod at Antioch where some were trying to establish Novatian's schism; McGiffert (note to VI.46) thinks Eusebius took it to have met and that it probably did; Hefele, Dittrich and others doubt it; Hefele will not rely on the Libellus Synodicus when it stands alone (npnf201 l.39010-39021; hefele_history v1 l.6492-6496)

contested_claims.claim: Whether Novatus of Carthage was one of the five presbyters condemned with Felicissimus
contested_claims.sides: Hefele I, sec. 5: not known, asserted by some and denied by others; Leclercq's note, after Paul Monceaux: he was one of the five

contested_claims.claim: How many councils met in 251 on the lapsed
contested_claims.sides: Hefele I, sec. 5: two, at Carthage and Rome; he says several editors of the acts and historians, misreading the documents, made them four

absent_details.note: The Carthage book of decisions is lost (Cyprian names it; Leclercq: nothing of this council remains). No acts of the Rome council are held; Eusebius summarises Cornelius's letters, which McGiffert notes are no longer extant.

absent_details.detail: The names and number of the bishops at Carthage in 251
absent_details.note: Cyprian says only 'a large number'. The synodal letter of the later council, to Cornelius, prints forty-one names in its ANF heading (anf05 l.34251-34257) and forty-two in the other texts given in its note (l.34263-34272); it belongs to that later council.
No source of the time gives them; May and October are Hefele's reconstruction, and Leclercq calls May certain after Monceaux.

absent_details.detail: Novatian's own account of the councils
absent_details.note: No letter of Novatian's on the councils is held. His rule comes through Socrates, and the Roman clergy letter Cyprian says he wrote comes before the councils.
